description: Change of use from Use Class C3 (dwelling house) to a Class Sui Generis (HMO - house in multiple occupation), increased ridge height, two storey side/front extension, rear dormers, construction of hard standing in connection with vehicular access, with associated amenity, cycle and refuse storage.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:SuDS Pro Forma,Scotland001 (Site Map),Scotland001 (Existing Drawings),Scotland002 (Proposed Drawings),Scotland006 (Block Plan as Proposed),Highway Safety Impact Form,Planning Statement Rev A,HMO Maintenance and Management Plan Rev 1.Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

Notwithstanding the details set out in the submitted preliminary drainage information (26_00185_FUL-Existing_and_Proposed_Plans-3244602 and 26_00185_FUL-SUDS_PRO_FORMA-3221952), October 2025, prior to the commencement of any construction work, details of the Sustainable Drainage Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and must conform with the Landscaping Strategy. The details shall include:' Sizes, storage volumes, cross-sections, long-sections (where appropriate) and specifications of all the source control SuDS measures including rain gardens, raised planters, green roofs, swale and permeable paving ' Final sizes, storage volumes, invert levels, cross-sections and specifications of all site control SuDS measures including ponds, soakaways and underground tanks. Include calculations demonstrating functionality where relevantReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the existing vehicular access has been reinstated at the expense of the applicant. This condition should be read in conjunction with the Informative (No. 3) also attached to the permission. Reason: In order to safeguard the character and appearance of the street scene, and provide adequate on street parking provision

Cycle parking shall be provided in accordance with the details provided within the submitted Highway Safety Impact Form, Planning Statement Rev A, and Drawing Reference: Scotland002 (Proposed Drawings) prior to the first occupation of the development hereby permitted. Cycle parking shall thereafter be retained in perpetuity, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Notwithstanding the details shown on the submitted drawings, prior to the first occupation of the HMO hereby permitted, waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers shall have been provided on site, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities are to be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.

Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved drawings, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details of hard and soft landscape works for the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Soft landscaping plans shall include planting plans (at a scale not less than 1:100), schedule of plants, noting species, plant sizes, plant containers (all at time of plating) and proposed numbers/densities and a landscape implementation programme. Hard landscaping works shall include: material details, full construction details (including cross sections) of permeable paving and their maintenance plan. All landscaping in accordance with the approved scheme shall be completed/planted during the first planting season following practical completion of the development hereby approved.  The landscaping details shall set out a plan for the continued management and maintenance of the site and any planting which dies, becomes severely damaged or diseased within five years of completion of the development shall be replaced with new planting in accordance with the approved details or an approved alternative and to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details as so approved prior to the first occupation of the development hereby permitted, and shall be maintained as such thereafter. Reason: To safeguard the appearance and character of the area, and to enhance the appearance of the development.

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby permitted, details on proposed means of enclosure across the full extent of the site shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall indicate the height, form and appearance of all forms of boundary treatment, including any new access gates.The approved means of enclosure shall be installed on site prior to the first occupation of the development, and shall thereafter be retained unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the appearance and character of the area, and in the interests of achieving sufficient

The HMO hereby permitted shall not be occupied by more than 8 residents at any one time, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  Reason: To ensure that the future occupation of the building does not compromise standards of accommodation and does not adversely affect the residential amenities of neighbouring properties.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms and the communal kitchen and dining room shall be retained in perpetuity. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.
